skills.name: Laws of thought in classical logic

note.text: Classical logic uses the laws of identity, non-contradiction and excluded middle. Identity keeps a thing or proposition itself: P is P. Non-contradiction says P and not P cannot both be true at the same time and in the same respect. Excluded middle says P or not P. It does not say that we know which is true. Changes of time or meaning can remove an apparent contradiction, so always state the conditions precisely. Other logical systems exist; this lesson uses the classical school framework.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: A Buea classroom door can be open in the morning and closed at night without contradiction. Claiming that it is fully open and not open at the same instant, using open in the same way, is different. Calling a business bank a river bank changes meaning; it cannot support an argument that depends on keeping bank fixed.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Write one proposition clearly before negating it. Keep its subject, time and meaning fixed. Distinguish a contradiction from a mere difference or lack of knowledge. In a computed truth exercise, evaluate the relationship rather than guessing from the number of words.
